name: IEC D flip-flop (rectangular form)
summary: IEC bistable with a dynamic C1 clock and a 1D data input, storing D on the active clock edge.
description: In IEC form the D flip-flop is an unlabelled bistable outline with a clock input labelled C1 carrying the dynamic wedge, and a data input labelled 1D to show it is controlled by C1. Asynchronous set and reset inputs are labelled S and R without a number. The two outputs are Q and its complement shown with a negation or polarity mark.

TI's overview stresses that a D input always sets the storage element to 1 at its internal 1 state and resets it at 0. On sequential drawings this form makes clocking explicit: anything without the 1 prefix acts immediately, regardless of the clock.
The symbol does not state setup, hold or propagation times, and does not define the power-up state unless an I=0 or I=1 qualifier is added.
readingNotes: The wedge on C1 indicates edge triggering.
S and R without numbers are asynchronous.
drawingChecklist: Label the clock C1 with a dynamic mark.
Add I=0 or I=1 where power-up state matters.
distinction: The IEC D latch has a C1 input without a dynamic mark and is transparent while C1 is active.
